items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: by that time I had really got indoctrinated with Louis to the point that I was going around trying to talk like him

ctx.x: man, he's stinkin' up the joint, hittin' all them high notes, trying to play like Louis Armstrong." When he came back, I was called me into his office, you know. He said, "Play like you play. Forget about them high notes." I just listened.

Sound(? ) good, man. You know, by that time I had really got indoctrinated with Louis to the point that I was going around trying to talk like him. You know, [POPS GROWL] "Yeah, urrgghh, yeah..." -- you know... And I went through that phase. But I never did get him so tight that I played exactly like him, you know.

You see, I think I was smart enough to know there were certain things I had to play to get through. Because I remember when my brother was trying to get me established around here, he had me in the Rhythm Club playing, you know, and I broke it up, but Chick Webb said, "He's fast but he ain't sayin' nothin'." That's the whole story, you dig. That's like I say, you get something, and you rehearse it and you rehearse it, and then you can play it fast and precisely. But what are you saying?
